# Let's verify the checksum algorithm with "LIC-44026-8830"
input_str = "LIC-44026-8830"
print(f"Length: {len(input_str)}")

# Based on the disassembly:
# rax starts at 1
# movzx edx, byte [rbx + rax - 1]  -> char at index (rax-1)
# lea esi, [rax + 1]  -> multiplier is (rax+1)
# rax goes from 1 to 14
# So: char[0] * 2 + char[1] * 3 + ... + char[13] * 15

checksum = 0
for i in range(14):
    char_val = ord(input_str[i])
    multiplier = i + 2  # i goes 0..13, so multiplier is 2..15
    checksum += char_val * multiplier
    print(f"i={i}, char='{input_str[i]}' ({char_val}), mult={multiplier}, product={char_val * multiplier}")

print(f"\nChecksum: {checksum} (hex: {hex(checksum)})")
print(f"Target: 10810 (hex: 0x2a3a)")
print(f"Match: {checksum == 0x2a3a}")

# Let me trace through the loop more carefully
# Initial: eax = 1, ecx = 0
# Loop body:
#   movzx edx, byte [rbx + rax - 1]  -> edx = char[rax-1]  (so char[0] when rax=1)
#   lea esi, [rax + 1]               -> esi = rax + 1      (so 2 when rax=1)
#   add rax, 1                       -> rax = rax + 1      (so 2 after first iter)
#   imul edx, esi                    -> edx = edx * esi
#   add ecx, edx                     -> ecx += edx
#   cmp rax, 0xf                     -> compare to 15
#   jne 0x4010d8                     -> loop if rax != 15

# So when rax=1: char[0] * 2
# When rax=2: char[1] * 3
# ...
# When rax=14: char[13] * 15
